angle_conventions.hip_sagittal_degrees: world sagittal thigh inclination from down: negative rearward; positive forward

sources.citation: Gatesy, Baeker and Hutchinson (2009), Constraint-based exclusion of limb poses for reconstructing theropod dinosaur locomotion
sources.scope: Comparative Tyrannosaurus rex MOR 555 model used geometric knee 30..180 and ankle 90..180 degree search intervals. This supports scalar coordinate sanity and the 180 degree straight endpoint; it is not measured Tarbosaurus ROM.

sources.citation: Eonwild Factory pre-existing gait engineering guardrails
sources.scope: Retains the existing global hip interval -45..80 degrees and knee minimum 65 degrees. Hip is a world thigh inclination, not a pelvis-relative anatomical joint coordinate.

sources.citation: Eonwild whole-cycle constrained and skinned candidate diagnostics
sources.scope: Tests feasible-first scalar enforcement, phase-pure recovery and final-GLB verification mechanics. Synthetic and authored evidence do not establish biological ROM.

limitations: No measured Tarbosaurus joint range of motion or in-vivo loading evidence is available.
Hip hard [-45,80] retains the existing factory engineering interval; preferred [-35,75] is an authored 10/5 degree operating margin, not anatomical certification.
Knee hard [65,180] retains the existing 65 degree engineering floor and uses the scalar metric's straight endpoint; preferred [68,175] is an authored 3/5 degree operating margin.
Ankle hard [90,180] uses a comparative-model-informed lower engineering guardrail and the scalar metric's straight endpoint; preferred [95,172] is an authored 5/8 degree operating margin.

A prior unbound diagnostic used a 178 degree knee and ankle ceiling without independent anatomical support and put loaded stance at that boundary; this profile uses the defined 180 degree straight endpoint instead.
Support and swing ranges are identical because phase-specific Tarbosaurus evidence is unresolved.
The profile is a scalar sagittal guardrail; it does not model 6DoF joints, force, muscle capacity, or translated bones.
